summary: The same III morphology has intransitive flight with an agent ending and transitive carrying off with an object. Overt l-marked subjects occur in both frames (PrS 51/14; PrS 28/18); l-marking alone does not identify a patient.

m-/me qum- supplies a flight source or adversary; l-/s- a destination. Willing elopement remains sense 2. Protective removal is grouped once as 2b, rather than separately by helper, escapee species or benevolent motivation.
New Preterit-wa examples independently establish anterior flight and abduction. komhazmole in 65/429 supports ko-Preterit from object -o and agent -le; no -wa is present.

The inherited Nomen Actionis box actually contains mahəzmone referring to fleeing persons. New parallel agent forms are provisionally kept in that same box, including mahzəmono with a d-marked abductee; no wholly new derivational pattern is claimed.

The Infinitiv covers both flight and abduction. təhzimo/tehzimo/tu hzimo vocalism varies in the supplied transcriptions; no normalization is imposed. Consent does not by itself establish a different sense.
78/179 may foreground rapid return, but the clause follows taking an object away and does not securely establish a separate meaning 'hurry'. Keep the inherited classification pending context review.
Do not infer rescue solely from consent or a police actor: Lahdo Traitor 1/45 and PrS 60/106 remain neutral caused-removal sense 2. The clear help-to-escape contexts establish 2b independently.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce round 2. All supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; analyses and sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Quoted English is copied verbatim and labelled as machine translation. Round-1 proposals are the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.

Flight remains III.1 even when military action, persecution or a sheikh's arrival supplies its cause. Mahzamme / mahzamwolle can have plural fleeing experiencers, including l-marked subjects; Jan 2.3/340 and 2.21/3916–3922 do not securely establish an external causer. The machine translation's transitive rendering is not independent evidence.

The apparent military-expulsion context at Jan 1.12/468 also permits ad dayroye as the subject of mahzamme. Jan 2.18/3727 introduces Petros's people before mahzamme and their several destinations; their own flight is possible. No new drive-away sense is published from these ambiguous frames.

Preterit-wa was already established in R1 for both flight and abduction; reader claims of a missing box are superseded. Jan mahzamwolən/mahzamwolle shows -wa plus the l-series, distinct from person-marked Infectum-wa mahzamnowo / mahzəminawo and transitive mahzəmiwole.

Jan 1.17/893 is best treated as carrying bread off with -le rather than a bare intransitive escape verb; the exact clitic referent still needs confirmation. Jan 1.51/2497 itself switches from carrying off livestock to wolves fleeing gunfire; individual tokens must be distinguished.

The bridal shoe passage Jan 1.38/1683 explains a local custom and has mahzəmonawo beside mahzamwo. It does not establish a fixed verb-plus-shoe idiom, and R1 has already retained the inherited Nomen Actionis heading for agentive forms.
No collocation is independently established beyond compositional flight from a source or carrying a theme away; no idiom has been added.
Confirm whether agentive mahəzmone/mahzəmono should retain the team's inherited Nomen Actionis heading or be relocated to Part act.; current additions deliberately follow the existing heading.

Resolve the agent/object segmentation of Mahzamla abre du baqoro (PrS 6/29), mahzamla under plural qayimi (PrS 16/20), and apparent gender mismatch in PrS 76/8. These are not quoted as paradigmatic evidence.
In 113/52, is the woman the subject or has the retelling changed the thief? The supplied verse and translation do not settle the earlier event.
Check German Entpflichtung at 29/104 and Lieb at 65/405 against the edition; neither is silently corrected or used for a new quotation.
Does 78/179 support pure rapid motion without escape? Check the related Infinitiv-only hmz entry for a possible root-order variant; no automatic duplicate-root merger is made.

In Jan 1.12/466,468, 2.3/340, 2.18/3727 and 2.21/3916–3922, does the verb mean the people fled, or an outside actor put them to flight? Confirm agent/object morphology before adding a causative sense.
Confirm -owalle / -owale in Jan 1.10/406 and 1.41/1835; both involve the abducted woman, but supplied oral morphology is uneven.
Does təhzimo d kallat in Jan 1.36/1448 specifically imply illegal smuggling or simply the constrained outward transfer? It remains an object-domain extension of III.2.
Confirm whether mahzəmiwole in Jan 1.17/893 contains the bread as its object; no new clitic construction is asserted.
Correct 'thas' to 'that'
rationale: English typo in She saw thas she could not escape.

summary: Animal subjects (cow, mare) and metaphorical smoke occur with the same intransitive flight frame.
The carried-off patient may be livestock, a cap, a sack, rope or dough. Treat patient changes as extensions of carrying off, not new numbered senses.
Jan independently supports R1's protective escape subsense: the children are carried away by their father, explicitly indexed by -lan. Do not propose this again as a new sense.

Carried-off themes include bread, a basket, a bridal shoe, bulgur, livestock and money. These continue R1's inanimate/animal extensions. Money transfer is constrained by the stated law; the verb alone does not prove illicit smuggling.
